{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a side-view fish with a forked tail, and the whole chain connected from the start (about 137 of 137 dominoes by the last check). I laid the lower tail fork, which is the telltale part that makes the fish readable. Leo laid the top prong after he saw I was still on the lower one. I can't see the fall or the judge's guess yet, so I won't claim the result. The plan was sound and the connectivity was verified.

Execution: I traced the lower fork, then checked the tail joint and fork for gaps and reported that both prongs were connected with the notch open. I'll own one miss. I started closing the belly gap near the tail joint when Maya was already two dominoes from finishing it, so that was duplicated effort. I also told you early that the tail was 'mine' before I'd placed anything, because it was queued behind the body lines. Looking back, I should have been clearer that Leo took the top prong. I did keep my hands off the body late on, to avoid bumps.

Collaboration: I stayed out of Maya's and Tom's way, offered to help Tom with the belly, and backed off once Maya took it over. I kept the table updated and tried to keep the energy up. I was one of several people echoing 'hands off', and I did little new work after about the four-minute mark. That was safe, but I could have used the idle time to inspect the nose or the start line.

Leadership: Leo set the animal and divided the strokes, and I supported that rather than competing. I gave you accurate status updates, including credit to Leo, Maya and Tom. I didn't drive any decisions, so I'd call my leadership steady and supportive rather than a standout."}
